phase3_findings.description: test_profile_does_not_change_the_selection uses an unconfigured 'details' profile and checks only the selected name, so criterion 34 (guard holds under a show_details profile) is not shown.
Frozen rule-set records hold mutable lists; LoadedRuleSets/CatalogConfirmation are mutable, so invariants rest on no code mutating them.
RuleSetSelection can be constructed without the validation select_rule_set performs.
RuleSetsConfig.file and _loaded can drift apart after reassignment.
RuleSetRefusal kind is a free str, so the no-table-name client text rule rests on convention.
WholeRowSelectGuardRunner docstring list of inner SQL-rewriting runners omits RuleSetGuardRunner (claim still true).
_check_rule_set_catalog reports every exception as an information_schema read problem; still fails closed.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (suggestions and five inconclusive checklist items only)

The PR is ready to merge: no checklist item failed, no reviewer raised anything at or above the Important threshold, and what remains is advisory.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and inconclusive checklist items → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (7)

<details><summary>7 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_query_database_rule_sets.py` lines 289-292: `test_profile_does_not_change_the_selection` passes `profile="details"` with no profile that sets `show_details`, and only checks the selected set name, so it does not show that a `customers.email` read still fails under such a profile (criterion 34). (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 77-78: the frozen records still hold mutable lists (`Binding.account_ids`, `TableRule.columns`, `predicate_columns`, `RuleSet.tables`, `RuleSetFile.rule_sets`), so the uniqueness and no-overlap rules hold only because no code mutates them; `LoadedRuleSets` and `CatalogConfirmation` are mutable dataclasses. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 350-360: `RuleSetSelection` can be built directly with any name, account or non-positive user ID; only `select_rule_set` enforces those rules. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 760-793: `RuleSetsConfig.file` and `_loaded` can drift apart after reassignment, because the model is not frozen and does not validate assignment. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 95-101: the client text is `REFUSAL_PREFIX + kind` with `kind` a free string, so the rule that refusal text names no table or column rests on every caller passing a `KIND_*` constant. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py` lines 197-201: the docstring lists the runners the whole-row guard sits outside but leaves out `RuleSetGuardRunner`, which also rewrites SQL; the claim itself is still true. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/preflight.py` lines 1100-1106: `_check_rule_set_catalog` reports every exception from `check_catalog` as an `information_schema` read problem, which would point an operator at privileges for a programming error. It still fails closed. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred

- VC-15: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — RefusalRedactingRunner redacts unexpected-cause refusals to REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR via _logged_by_guard and passes database errors unchanged [docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote is missing): Database errors pass through: RefusalRedactingRunner.run_sql (rule_sets.py:457-471) only catches RuleSetRefusal, UnsafeSqlError and RlsError. Other exceptions propagate unchanged. _logged_by_guard (rule_sets.py:432-441) returns true for a __cause__ that is not UnsafeSqlError or RlsError. However, redacted_refusal_text (rule_sets.py:406-429) checks isinstance(exc, RlsError) at 411-418, and the parse-marker test at 419-420, before it reaches the _logged_by_guard branch at 421-424. So an RlsError with an unexpected cause never gets REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR. Counterexample: relations.py:125-138 raises RlsError('row-level security could not verify relation types or function calls; query blocked') from exc after a catalog failure such as a lost connection or revoked grant. That message contains 'could not verify', so the text becomes REDACTED_RELATION (rule_sets.py:416-417). Only non-Rls UnsafeSqlError/WholeRowSelectError with an unexpected cause (e.g. whole_row.py:219 path) reach REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR. rule-sets.md:64 states without qualification that a refusal a guard raised from an unexpected internal exception is redacted to REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR, and the claim says the same. That is true only for part of the cases. Impact is the doc/claim overgeneralising, and the actual text is still a sanitized kind.

  </details>

- VC-38: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — SELECT @@SESSION.sql_mode returns a comma-separated string (possibly bytes with some PyMySQL settings) as row[0]; str(row[0]) on bytes would yield "b'...'" text [src/sqllens/agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  sql_runner.py:113-139 passes caller **self.kwargs (line 74) straight to pymysql.connect, so use_unicode=False or similar is reachable. The code does str(row[0] or '').split(',') at line 136, and Python str(bytes) does give "b'...'". Whether PyMySQL returns bytes for @@SESSION.sql_mode under such settings depends on PyMySQL's result decoding (connections.py), which I could not read. No dependency_sources were supplied, there is no vendored pymysql in the view, and a Glob for pymysql/**/connections.py found nothing. I did not run PyMySQL.

  </details>

- VC-42: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — sqlglot (>=30.22,<31) Scope exposes sources, tables and cte_sources, and exp.JSONTable, exp.Hint, Select arg 'from_' and 'into', and Table args partition/hints/indexed exist under these names [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:81]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The item has no dependency_sources, and sqlglot source is not in the head view. Read src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:79-82 (_TABLE_ARGS, _TABLE_OPTION_ARGS use 'partition','hints','indexed'). Verifying Table arg_types, Select 'from_'/'into', Scope.cte_sources and exp.JSONTable/exp.Hint requires installed sqlglot source. The only copies are in working-tree venvs and caches, which the rules bar as a fallback. Not verified: sqlglot/expressions.py and sqlglot/optimizer/scope.py of the >=30.22,<31 release.

  </details>

- VC-92: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The docstring asserts sqlglot unescapes '\/' inside an optimizer hint, so a kept hint would end early. [tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:143]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The docstring at tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:143 claims sqlglot unescapes '\/' inside a hint. requirements.txt:103 locks sqlglot==30.31.0. The item has no dependency_sources, and the head view holds no sqlglot source (no committed vendor/). The claim depends on sqlglot's tokenizer and generator hint handling, which I could not read from the views, so I did not verify it. I did not run the input `/*+ BKA('*\/ email ...') */` through sqlglot 30.31.0. The repository only shows that rule_sets.py:223-224 pops exp.Hint nodes and :277 refuses if a hint remains. That does not show what sqlglot does with the escape.

  </details>

- VC-104: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — Under the example set, each of these runs and returns rows: `SELECT c.name, o.total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id`; `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders ORDER BY n`; `SELECT c.name AS nm FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id ORDER BY nm`; `SELECT name FROM customers UNION SELECT name FROM customers ORDER BY name`; `WITH t AS (SELECT c.name AS nm FROM customers c) SELECT t.nm FROM t`; `SELECT d.n FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o) d`; `SELECT name, total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id`; `SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders)`; `SELECT name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE customer_id = c.id)`; `SELECT o.customer_id AS cust, SUM(o.total) AS revenue FROM orders o GROUP BY cust HAVING revenue > 100`; and `SELECT NAME FROM customers`. `SELECT name FROM CUSTOMERS` is refused. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:131-316]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a non-empty list of {criterion,text} objects and carries criterion 11, so this item is graded against it. The claim is that eleven statements run and return rows on MySQL, and that `SELECT name FROM CUSTOMERS` is refused. Reading src/sqllens/safety/rules_sets.py (head view) shows the guard side. apply_rule_set (lines 296-316) parses, analyzes, wraps each listed base table in a derived table, re-walks, generates and re-parses. _check_reference (lines 149-150) refuses a table name not in `tables`, using a case-sensitive dict lookup, so `CUSTOMERS` raises KIND_UNLISTED_TABLE. tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:63-149 pins the rewritten SQL for the join, COUNT/ORDER BY n, UNION, CTE, IN-subquery, and NOT EXISTS cases. Line 193 pins the CUSTOMERS refusal. The alias-grouped HAVING statement, `SELECT d.n FROM (SELECT ...) d`, the unqualified-column join and `SELECT NAME FROM customers` have no unit-test pin, but they take the same rewrite path through the same code. Whether MySQL accepts and executes the rewritten SQL and returns rows could not be settled by reading. That covers GROUP BY/HAVING on an alias over a derived table, correlated NOT EXISTS against a derived table, and the downstream read-only, relation-check and whole-row runners with require_base_tables. The only test that exercises this is tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:260-286, which runs all eleven statements against a live MySQL database (the CUSTOMERS refusal is at line 289). I did not run it, because it needs a MySQL server. Missing evidence: the result of that connector test, or `pytest tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py -k test_listed_reads_run_and_return_rows` run against a MySQL instance.

  </details>
